skill.name: chronicle-assistant-guide
skill.description: Guides AI assistants to use Chronicle project memory through search-first workflows, MCP tools, CLI fallback commands, roadmap checks, and session history review.
skill.summary: Search Chronicle history, roadmap data, and session summaries before assistant work.
skill.author: ChandlerHardy

security_audit.summary: The static command findings are false positives from Markdown inline code, code fences, and Chronicle CLI examples. The hidden-file and SQLite findings are documentation of Chronicle storage paths, not direct file access. A semantic privacy issue remains because the guide encourages broad Chronicle searches across all projects without requiring scoping or consent.

remediation.issue: Overbroad Chronicle searches can expose unrelated session history.
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance to prefer repo_path filters and ask before searching across projects or personal transcripts.
Document that Chronicle results may include sensitive local work and should be summarized only when relevant.

semantic_findings.title: Overbroad Local History Search Scope
semantic_findings.description: The guide says it works across all projects and tells assistants to search Chronicle history before tasks. Without a required project filter or consent step, broad searches can expose unrelated local session records in the current conversation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited lines explicitly set all-project scope and recommend searches without required filters. The issue is privacy exposure, not evidence of external exfiltration.

content.value_statement: AI assistants lose time when they ignore prior Chronicle sessions and roadmap context. This skill guides them to search history, choose MCP or CLI, and reuse project knowledge.
actual_capabilities: Directs assistants to search Chronicle history before Chronicle-related work.
Shows MCP and CLI options for sessions, commits, roadmap, and milestones.
Provides workflows for starting tasks, debugging issues, and understanding project history.
Explains when to prefer MCP tools and when to use CLI fallback.
Lists common mistakes, quick reference commands, and Chronicle storage locations.
limitations: Requires Chronicle, its MCP server, or its CLI to be installed separately.
Does not install, configure, or repair Chronicle by itself.
Search quality depends on the completeness of stored Chronicle sessions and summaries.
Broad searches can surface sensitive local history if users do not scope queries.

use_cases.title: Recover Past Implementation Context
use_cases.description: Search prior sessions before editing similar code, then reuse successful approaches and avoid repeated mistakes.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Roadmap Work
use_cases.description: Review milestones and pending steps before creating new tasks or changing project direction.

use_cases.title: Debug Recurring Issues
use_cases.description: Find earlier symptoms, fixes, and failed attempts before proposing a new debugging plan.

prompt_templates.title: Find Related History
prompt_templates.prompt: Search Chronicle for prior work on [topic]. Summarize the most relevant sessions before suggesting next steps.

prompt_templates.title: Check Planned Work
prompt_templates.prompt: Check Chronicle roadmap and pending next steps for [project]. Tell me what is already planned before we create new work.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate A Bug
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Chronicle to investigate [bug or symptom]. Compare past fixes, failed attempts, and current roadmap items before proposing a fix.

prompt_templates.title: Build A Context Brief
prompt_templates.prompt: Combine Chronicle session search, commit search, and roadmap review for [initiative]. Produce a scoped implementation brief with risks and dependencies.

output_examples.input: I need to debug recurring MCP response size problems.
output_examples.output: The assistant first searches Chronicle for response size and MCP sessions. It summarizes earlier fixes, then recommends a focused debugging plan.

output_examples.input: Help me start work on authentication cleanup.
output_examples.output: The assistant checks Chronicle history and roadmap items for authentication. It reports related sessions, open steps, and likely duplication risks.

output_examples.input: What changed in the project last week?
output_examples.output: The assistant reviews Chronicle timeline, commits, and session summaries. It returns a concise progress summary with unresolved follow-up work.

best_practices: Search Chronicle before implementation, debugging, or roadmap changes.
Use MCP tools when available, and use CLI commands when MCP is not configured.
Filter by project, date, tool, or topic when broad history is not needed.
anti_patterns: Starting Chronicle-related work without searching prior sessions.
Reading unrelated session history when a scoped query would be enough.
Treating generated summaries as final proof without checking relevant details.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps assistants use Chronicle history, roadmap data, and session summaries before they act.

faq.question: Does it require the Chronicle MCP server?
faq.answer: No. It prefers MCP when available, but it also documents CLI fallback workflows.

faq.question: Can it install Chronicle?
faq.answer: No. It is guidance only and assumes Chronicle tools already exist in the environment.

faq.question: What tools does it mention?
faq.answer: It covers Chronicle MCP tools and Chronicle CLI commands for sessions, commits, milestones, and roadmap data.

faq.question: Is it useful outside one repository?
faq.answer: Yes. The guide is project-agnostic, but users should scope searches to avoid unrelated history.

faq.question: Does it change project data?
faq.answer: Most guidance is read-focused, but it also documents commands that can update milestones and next steps.
